auto_merge.commit_title: gh-142557: fix UAF in `bytearray.__mod__` when object is mutated while formatting `%`-style arguments (#143213)

files.patch:
@@ -1382,6 +1382,18 @@ def test_bytearray_api(self):
             except OSError:
                 pass
 
+    def test_mod_concurrent_mutation(self):
+        # Prevent crash in __mod__ when formatting mutates the bytearray.
+        # Regression test for https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/142557.
+        fmt = bytearray(b"%a end")
+
+        class S:
+            def __repr__(self):
+                fmt.clear()
+                return "E"
+
+        self.assertRaises(BufferError, fmt.__mod__, S())
+
     def test_reverse(self):
         b = bytearray(b'hello')
         self.assertEqual(b.reverse(), None)

@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+Fix a use-after-free crash in :ref:`bytearray.__mod__ <bytes-formatting>` when
+the :class:`!bytearray` is mutated while formatting the ``%``-style arguments.
+Patch by Bénédikt Tran.

review_comments.body:
This can happen not when the `__repr__()` method mutates the bytearray, but when it is mutated (most likely in other thread, can can also be triggered by GC) during execution of the `__repr__()` method. And not only, but `__index__()`, `__float__()` and other overridable special methods. `__repr__()` is just an example used for easy reproducing the issue.

So remove mention of concrete `__repr__()`, and use "mutated during formatting of the arguments" or something like.

@@ -1382,6 +1382,19 @@ def test_bytearray_api(self):

+    def test_mod_use_after_free(self):
+        # Prevent UAF in bytearray % (a1, a2) with re-entrant a[12].__repr__.
review_comments.body: "Re-entrant" is a wrong term. It is not re-entered here, and the issue not specific to `__repr__`. This is a concurrency issue, not re-entrancy issue.
